title: San Francisco’s redevelopment wind-down left two staff to handle financial reporting

beats.text: When San Francisco dissolved its redevelopment agency, financial reporting still had to happen.

visual.sub: Five financial reporting staff became two at dissolution

beats.text: Five people had handled it before dissolution. Two remained afterward.
Balances still had to be reconciled and financial statements prepared.

visual.kicker: Five financial reporting staff became two at dissolution

beats.text: Independent auditors classified the staffing problem as a material weakness.

visual.kicker: Five financial reporting staff became two at dissolution

beats.text: The successor agency described a budget of about $300 million.

visual.kicker: The remaining staff faced financial obligations beyond the operating budget

beats.text: Most of that covered debt service and bond proceeds.

visual.kicker: The remaining staff faced financial obligations beyond the operating budget

beats.text: The administrative budget was about $10 million.
A Controller’s Office director took a finance assignment at the agency.

visual.kicker: The remaining staff faced financial obligations beyond the operating budget

beats.text: The next external audit checked what happened after the transfer.

visual.kicker: The next external audit found the weakness corrected

beats.text: Auditors saw no similar reporting problem in the following year.

visual.kicker: The next external audit found the weakness corrected

beats.text: They considered the finding corrected. No cash loss was documented.
